title: Improved Methods for Acetocarmine and Haematoxylin Staining to Visualize Chromosomes in Zygnema
author: Nina Rittmeier
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Chromosomes (circles) visualized by light microscopy in different Zygnema strains. (A, D, G) Z. cylindricum ; (B, E, H) Z. circumcarinatum; and (C, F, I) Z. Saalach. (A, B, C) Living cells without staining; (D, E, F) acetocarmine staining; (G, H, I) haematoxylin staining. Insets in E, G, and I show manual drawings of chromosomes counted with ImageJ; counted chromosome numbers: n = 20 for Z. cylindricum/Z. circumcarinatum and n = 30 for Z. Saalach. Scale bars = 20 µm. Zygnema circumcarinatum strain SAG 698-1b ( Figure 2B ; isolated 1929 by Czurda V.; deposited 1954 by Pringshein E.G.), collected from a ditch at meadow Poselteich (Polenský Rybnik; 50°33′09.7"N 14°40′09.7″E) near Hirschberg (Dosky) in Czech Republic, Europe. steps.title: Prepare 2 mM 8‑Hydroxyquinoline
steps.instruction: Dissolve 29 mg 8‑hydroxyquinoline in 1 000 mL bi‑distilled water (A. bidest) to obtain a 2 mM solution; store in the dark at room temperature (RT) for up to 1 year and for up to 100 preparations.

steps.title: Prepare Carnoy’s fluid
steps.instruction: Mix 125 mL glacial acetic acid (100 %) with 375 mL absolute ethanol (100 %) to a total volume of 500 mL; prepare immediately before use and it can be used for up to 50 preparations.

steps.title: Prepare aceto‑haematoxylin‑iron alum
steps.instruction: Combine 100 mL 45 % acetic acid, 400 mg haematoxylin (0.4 %) and 100 mg ammonium iron(III) sulfate (0.1 %) to a final volume of 100 mL; store at 4 °C for up to 6 months and for up to 300 preparations.

steps.title: Grow cultures for acetocarmine
steps.instruction: Place pure Zygnema biomass into a 250–500 mL Erlenmeyer flask with 150–250 mL Bold’s basal medium (BBM); incubate under a 10 h light/14 h dark cycle at 20 °C with 50 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ for 2–3 weeks until log‑phase is reached.

steps.title: Harvest biomass for acetocarmine
steps.instruction: At the start of the dark cycle, collect algae in a laminar‑flow hood, transfer each sample with fine‑pointed tweezers into a 2 mL tube containing 1 mL A. bidest at RT.

steps.title: Fix acetocarmine samples
steps.instruction: Transfer each tube to a 10 mL glass vial with 5 mL 2 mM 8‑hydroxyquinoline; incubate at RT for 1–2 h, then at 4 °C for 1–2 h (species‑specific: 1 h for SAG 698‑1a/1b, 2 h for SAG 2419). Remove the quinoline with a glass Pasteur pipette and wash three times with 5 mL A. bidest (≥1 min each) under the fume hood.

steps.title: Bleach samples in Carnoy’s fluid
steps.instruction: Immediately submerge the washed samples in 5 mL Carnoy’s fluid and leave at RT for 12 h until chlorophyll is removed and the material appears visibly bleached.

steps.title: Acetocarmine staining and mounting
steps.instruction: Collect the bleached filaments with tweezers, place them in a test tube containing 5 mL 1 % acetocarmine, hold the tube with a wooden clip over a low‑flame gas burner and boil for 5 min under the fume hood. Transfer the boiled material to a culture dish, pick stained filaments, mount on a microscope slide with a small droplet of acetocarmine and cover with a coverslip.

steps.title: Microscopy and chromosome counting (acetocarmine)
steps.instruction: Observe the slides with a light microscope, acquire 50–100 Z‑stack images per area (step size 0.2–0.4 µm), render stacks with Helicon Focus, and count chromosomes in ImageJ using background subtraction, thresholding, binary processing, fill‑holes, watershed and particle analysis. Count at least three biological replicates (≥10 technical replicates per replicate).

steps.title: Grow cultures for haematoxylin
steps.instruction: Place pure Zygnema biomass into 250–500 mL tubes containing 200 mL BBM; incubate under a 10 h light/14 h dark cycle at 20 °C with 50 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ for at least 2 weeks.

steps.title: Harvest biomass for haematoxylin
steps.instruction: At the beginning of the dark cycle, collect algae in a laminar‑flow hood and transfer each sample with fine‑pointed tweezers into a 2 mL tube containing 1 mL A. bidest at RT.

steps.title: Fix haematoxylin samples and ethanol storage
steps.instruction: Place the harvested material into a 10 mL glass vial with 5 mL Carnoy’s fluid and incubate at RT for 2 h or until completely bleached. Decant the fluid, add 5 mL 70 % ethanol (samples can be stored at 4 °C for up to 6 months). Wash three times with 5 mL A. bidest (≥1 min each).

steps.title: Mount and squash slides in 45 % acetic acid
steps.instruction: Transfer the washed, bleached material onto a microscope slide, add a drop of 45 % acetic acid, place a second slide on top and gently squash the filaments.

steps.title: Freeze slides in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Fill a liquid‑nitrogen container halfway, wear goggles, leather gloves and a spray skirt, open the lid, dip the two slides for 10 s using long tongs, remove, pull the slides apart while still frozen, and let them air‑dry for ≥30 min; allow residual liquid nitrogen to evaporate under the fume hood.

steps.title: HCl treatment of slides
steps.instruction: Immerse each dried slide in 5 N HCl for ≥10 min under the fume hood, then air‑dry for an additional 30 min. Stain immediately or store the slides in a glass jar at –20 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Stain with aceto‑haematoxylin‑iron alum
steps.instruction: Apply one droplet of the aceto‑haematoxylin‑iron alum solution onto the slide, place a coverslip, and incubate for 5 min for full saturation; remove excess dye with lint‑free paper. Use a syringe with a filter to avoid particulate contamination.

steps.title: Microscopy and chromosome counting (haematoxylin)
steps.instruction: Observe the stained slides with a light microscope, acquire up to 100 Z‑stack images per area, render stacks with Helicon Focus, and count chromosomes in ImageJ using the same processing pipeline as for acetocarmine. Use at least three biological replicates (≥10 technical replicates per replicate).
